title: Microsoft Purview: Adaptive Protection retains content deleted by high-risk users (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the documented commercial-cloud controls and behaviour. It clearly distinguishes the planned government release from commercial documentation and reports the unresolved government availability, default and licensing details.

claims.claim: The planned integration automatically applies retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on insider risk level.
claims.quote: The integration with Data Lifecycle Management will automatically apply retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user’s insider risk level.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection moves users into and out of policies as their insider risk levels change.
claims.quote: integrating dynamic insider risk levels, determined by data related activities, with various policy engines to automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk levels change over time

claims.claim: The tenant retention toggle is in the Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Settings > Solution settings > Data lifecycle management > Adaptive protection > Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Settings > Solution settings> Data lifecycle management > Adaptive protection.
2. For Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management, turn the setting off

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API is documented for the Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Adaptive protection" "Data Lifecycle" "PowerShell"; "AdaptiveProtection" in PowerShell; "Adaptive protection" "Graph" "settings" enable. Opened Learn retention, retention-cmdlets and insider-risk-management-adaptive-protection; no operation for this switch found.

claims.claim: The data lifecycle setting can be enabled only while Adaptive Protection is enabled for the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to turn on this setting unless Adaptive Protection is turned on for your tenant.

claims.claim: Turning off the data lifecycle setting deletes its policy.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, the data lifecycle management policy is deleted.

claims.claim: Turning off the data lifecycle setting removes the labels applied by Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote: Any retention labels that were applied as a result of Adaptive Protection are removed so that the items can then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: Removing those labels makes the items eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Any retention labels that were applied as a result of Adaptive Protection are removed so that the items can then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: The tenant Adaptive Protection toggle is in the Microsoft Purview portal at Insider Risk Management > Adaptive protection > Adaptive Protection settings > Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote:
Go to the Insider Risk Management solution.
3. Select Adaptive protection in the left navigation
To enable Adaptive Protection, select the Adaptive Protection settings tab, and then turn Adaptive Protection to On.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API is documented for enabling or disabling Adaptive Protection itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "AdaptiveProtection" in PowerShell; "Adaptive protection" "Graph" "settings" enable; "Adaptive Protection" "insider risk levels" "API" settings. Opened insider-risk-management-adaptive-protection and returned setup excerpts; no switch operation found.

claims.claim: On the Custom insider risk level pane, Insider risk level based on offers Alert generated or confirmed for a user and Specific user activity.

On the Custom insider risk level pane, select an option in the Insider risk level based on section:

claims.claim: Audit searches are available in the Microsoft Purview portal at Audit > Search.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select the Audit solution card.
3. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -Operations <operation names> searches the unified audit log by date and operation.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    [-Operations <String[]>]
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: Searching audit logs requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: The audit command reads events rather than configuring retention.
claims.quote: Use the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet to search the unified audit log.

claims.claim: The commercial quick-setup table says the data lifecycle policy is automatically created and applied when Adaptive Protection is first enabled.
claims.quote: If you haven't already turned on Adaptive Protection, the policy is automatically created and applied when you turn on Adaptive Protection.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale
claims.claim: The documented commercial integration retains qualifying deleted content for 120 days.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: The documented integration covers content deleted from SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented retention trigger is users assigned the Elevated insider risk level by Adaptive Protection.
claims.quote: Preserve any SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange Online content deleted by a risky user for 120 days. A risky user in this case is a user that Adaptive Protection assigns the Elevated risk level.

claims.claim: The automatic retention label applies to previously unlabelled content.
claims.quote: retention labels are automatically applied to unlabeled content if it's deleted by users who have been identified as an elevated risk

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Retained deleted content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery in the workload's secured locations.
claims.quote: As a result, that content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery from the secured locations used by the workload.

claims.claim: After the 120 days expire, retained items become eligible for permanent deletion rather than necessarily being immediately deleted.
claims.quote: After the 120 days expire, the items then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: The Learn retention page marks this integration as preview.
claims.quote: In preview, you can use this solution with Insider Risk Management so that retention labels are automatically applied with Adaptive Protection.

claims.claim: The documented integration uses a single retention label for the tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The documented integration uses a single auto-labeling retention policy for the tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Users do not see the integration's retention label.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: The generated label and policy are not visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The retention label and auto-labeling policy are supplied automatically rather than requiring administrators to create and manage them.
claims.quote: you don't need to create or manage the retention label or auto-labeling retention policy

claims.claim: The documented commercial retention period cannot currently be changed.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period

claims.claim: The documented commercial integration cannot currently assign different retention policies for different risk levels.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: The documented commercial integration cannot currently assign different retention policies for different locations.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: The Preservation Hold library counts against site storage quota, so SharePoint and OneDrive retention may require more storage.
claims.quote: Because the Preservation Hold library is included in the site's storage quota, you might need to increase your storage when you use retention settings for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Disabling Adaptive Protection stops assigning and sharing insider risk levels with data lifecycle management without automatically deleting the policy.
claims.quote:
the system stops assigning insider risk levels to users and stops sharing them with data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access.
The Insider Risk Management, data loss prevention, data lifecycle management, and Conditional Access policies aren't automatically deleted.

claims.quote: Depending on the Insider Risk Management policy assigned in Adaptive Protection, different criteria (users, groups, indicators, thresholds, etc.) are used to determine applicable insider risk levels.
